To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the adenovirus oncogene E1A induces the activation of caspases in extracts from drug- resistant cells, 2) the E1A oncogenes induce the generation of an OGA that activates caspases in drug-resistant cells, 3) partially purified OGA from drug-resistant cells induces the activation of ICE-like proteases and apoptosis in extracts from normal cells.
extracts from drug-resistant 293 cells contain an activator of caspases that is generated by E1A and can induce apoptosis in a drug-resistant cell line.

1) the drug resistant 293 cell line does not respond to an anticancer drug by activating the caspase proteases that mediate apoptosis, 2) extracts from untreated 293 cells contain a factor that activates caspases and induces apoptosis in a cell free system, 3) this factor is not present in extracts of normal cells, and 4) partially purified factor activates caspases in extracts from untransformmed cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel cancer therapeutics.
the development of new agents that can selectively kill tumor cells and spare normal tissues.
the mechanisms of apoptosis, the process by which cells kill themselves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the drug-resistant cancer cell line has the machinery for apoptosis but not its activator.

the E1A oncogenic protein is able to activate the apoptotic pathway in cancer cells and that the use of this pathway as a target for cancer therapy is a novel approach that could be effective for the treatment of a variety of cancers.
this study provides the first evidence that an oncogene generates an activator of the apoptotic pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oncogene-generated activities can be harnessed to kill tumor cells.
we have found a novel mechanism by which tumor cells can become resistant to apoptosis and we have developed a novel approach that can be used to overcome this resistance.
we have discovered a novel mechanism of apoptosis induction in cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oncogene-induced apoptosis may not be restricted to cells with oncogenic mutations but could be induced in normal cells by oncogene products.

the oncogene E1A, which is present in many human tumors, activates the apoptotic machinery in a cell-free extract system and that the same oncogene may activate the apoptotic machinery of cancer cells in vivo.
the oncogene E1A generates a novel activity, OGA, that is responsible for the apoptosis in extracts from transformed cells.
